raw_segments.text: To whose bright image nightly by the moon Sidonian virgins paid their vows and songs.
In Sian also not unsung, where stood her temple on T.H., offensive mountain, built by that
oxorious king whose heart, though large beguiled by fair idolatresses, fell to idol's fowl.
Tomos came next behind, whose annual wound in Lebanon allured the Syrian damsels to lament
his fate in amorous ditties all a summer's day, while smooth Adonis from his native rock
ran purple to the sea, supposed with blood of Tomos' yearly wounded.
The love-tail infected Sian's daughters with like heat, whose wanton passions and the sacred
porch Ezekiel saw, when, by the vision led, his eye surveyed the dark idolatries of alienated
